Refugees, wounded people and guards competed for limited food and labor.

Variants.Content: Sandomierz suffered during the Mongol invasion of 1241. Roads and places of refuge near the Vistula mattered to inhabitants. Fugitives needed family, food and animals moved, while defenders balanced incoming people against limited stores.

Sandomierz suffered during the Mongol invasion of 1241. Roads and places of refuge near the Vistula mattered to inhabitants. Fugitives needed family, food and animals moved, while defenders balanced incoming people against limited stores. Defenders rotated rest, watches and repairs, while sorties exposed those outside. Besiegers also needed food and fodder; weather and delay burdened both sides.

Sandomierz suffered during the Mongol invasion of 1241. Roads and places of refuge near the Vistula mattered to inhabitants. Fugitives needed family, food and animals moved, while defenders balanced incoming people against limited stores. Commanders weighed stores, relief and endurance before holding or negotiating. A promised army was not a delivered grain cart, and repaired walls did not replace food.

Fugitives needed family, food and animals moved, while defenders balanced incoming people against limited stores. Families allocated food, water and shelter from fire, burdening hosts in crowded quarters. Refugees still worried over abandoned fields, animals and houses.
